lines.text: Many learners say: I bought a book at the library.
Better: I bought a book at the bookstore.
A library lends books. A bookstore sells books.
Bookstore! I go to the bookstore.

data.wrong: I bought a book at the library.
data.right: I bought a book at the bookstore.
data.why: A library lends books. A bookstore sells books.

quiz.stem: I pay money for a new book. I go to the ___.

native.tip: En anglais, “library” veut dire « bibliothèque ». Pour « librairie », dites “bookstore”.
native.caption: Vous dites “I bought a book at the library.” ? “Library” veut dire « bibliothèque », pas « librairie ». Pour un magasin de livres, dites “bookstore”. Dites plutôt “I bought a book at the bookstore.” — écoutez Carlos et répétez avec lui ! Plus d’exercices dans l’appli Lexkite.

en.tip: In English, “library” is where you borrow books. For a shop that sells books, say “bookstore”.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I bought a book at the library.” In English, “library” is where you borrow books. For a shop that sells books, say “bookstore”. Say “I bought a book at the bookstore.” Listen to Carlos and repeat with him! More exercises in the Lexkite app.
